gaps.reason:
FAPI 2.0 makes PAR mandatory, so /authorize refuses a direct request
with oneauth's error page. The harness asks for a screenshot of it.

A request_uri is single-use (RFC 9126 §2.2), so the second visit gets
oneauth's error page. The harness asks for a screenshot of it.

An expired request_uri gets oneauth's error page. The harness asks for
a screenshot of it.

A request_uri presented with another client's client_id gets oneauth's
error page. The harness asks for a screenshot of it.

The harness runs this only with an RSA client key, and the plan's
clients use ES256 because oneauth can't register a PS256 client yet
(issue 330). The harness says the skip doesn't block certification.

oneauth's ID tokens carry a `typ: ID` claim so a resource server
refuses one presented as an access token (checkAccessTokenKind), the
marker Keycloak uses too. OIDC defines no marker, and a JOSE header
typ other than JWT is refused by common relying-party libraries
(Nimbus), so the claim stays and the harness warns that the client
did not request it.

Discovery advertises claims_parameter_supported and the ID token
carries every requested claim the user has, but also oneauth's typ: ID
marker claim, which the harness doesn't know. Issue 339 kept the
marker, as for the happy-flow module.

A request without redirect_uri gets oneauth's error page (OIDC Core
§3.1.2.1 makes it required), and the harness asks for a screenshot.

An unregistered redirect URI gets oneauth's error page, never a
redirect (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1). The harness asks for a screenshot of it.

The outer redirect_uri is unregistered and the registered one is inside
a request object, which oneauth doesn't read (JAR, issue 338). So it
shows its request_not_supported error page instead of redirecting, and
the harness asks for a screenshot of it.

oneauth never issues unsigned ID tokens (alg none), so discovery
doesn't offer it and the harness skips the module.

A login older than max_age sends the user back to the login page
(issue 453), and the harness asks for a screenshot of it.

prompt=login sends the logged-in user back to the login page (issue
453), and the harness asks for a screenshot of that second login page.

The redirect_uri adds a query the registered one doesn't have, so it
doesn't match. oneauth shows its error page, and the harness asks for a
screenshot of it.

The redirect_uri's query differs from the registered one, so it doesn't
match. oneauth shows its error page, and the harness asks for a
screenshot of it.

The harness asks a person to check the consent page shows the client's
logo. It does (issue 507), and the evidence checks the captured page.

The harness asks a person to check the consent page shows the client's
link to its policy. It does (issue 507), and the evidence checks the captured page.

The harness asks a person to check the consent page shows the client's
link to its terms. It does (issue 507), and the evidence checks the captured page.

oneauth doesn't support request objects, so discovery has no
request_object_signing_alg_values_supported. That's JAR, issue 338.

oneauth refuses request_uri with request_uri_not_supported. Request
objects by reference are JAR, issue 338.

The ID token carries oneauth's typ: ID marker claim, which stops it
validating as an access token. Issue 339 kept it as a claim: a JOSE
typ header other than JWT is refused by common relying-party
libraries. Issue 480 confirmed that, so the warning stays.

oneauth refuses request objects with request_not_supported (OIDC Core
§6.1), and the harness reports that rejection as SKIPPED. Supporting
request objects is JAR, issue 338.

The harness puts response_mode=form_post and state only inside the
request object. oneauth doesn't read request objects, so it refuses
with request_not_supported in the response type's default mode, and
the module fails CheckCallbackHttpMethodIsPost. The Basic OP and
Implicit OP plans report the same refusal as SKIPPED. Reading request
objects is JAR, issue 338.

The server-auth scenarios test a resource server, and they don't drive
/authorize, so they can't see the RFC 9207 iss in the redirect. The AS
does advertise it (auth-iss-param-as-metadata-advertises-support
passes). The mcp-auth-as run checks the redirect itself:
authorization-code-grant requires an iss that matches the issuer.

oneauth's AS doesn't accept Client ID Metadata Documents as client_id
yet, so its metadata doesn't advertise
client_id_metadata_document_supported. The MCP spec makes it a SHOULD.
